title: Survey hopping and erasure-code candidates
description:
Review documented software-hopping and across-fragment erasure-code designs before proposing new code. Shortlist exact code constructions with recoverability conditions, parameter bounds, metadata requirements, memory and encode/decode costs, independent vectors and reuse restrictions.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Read-only prior-art and feasibility research. No new dependency, code import, vendor contact or purchase. Any selected implementation or restricted reuse must be within the explicit microfrag.06 human-approved prototype scope.
acceptance_criteria: Each candidate has a primary reference and an explicit distinction between erasure recovery, corruption detection and authentication. Explain why rate 1/2 does not alone guarantee recovery from any half of fragments. Report unsuitable candidates and licensing questions without selecting a license workaround or claiming novelty.
